description: Replace the accepted candidate's prefix, producer and public-endpoint gaps using real four-node histories. Compare old VerifyLeader after a newer leader completes a command with and without connectivity to the nonvoter. Observe completed futures and raw FSM values; the controller applies an independent no-success-after-supersession oracle.

harness.description: TestAssuranceVerifyAuthorityHistory: independent with_nonvoter and without_nonvoter_contact subtests, real bootstrap/elections/membership/application, controlled route cuts, then public VerifyLeader.Error.
semantic_changes: A transport wrapper counts successful real AppendEntries returns without modifying requests or responses.
The wrapper declines the optional pipeline with ErrPipelineReplicationNotSupported; ordinary replication is retained.
MockFSM is the repository implementation and is read under its mutex; no FSM mutation is injected.
Nonuniform but individually validated node-local timeouts create a finite observation window while every lease/election worker remains active.
No target source or dependency definitions are changed.

legality.derivation: O-verify-current-authority is tested through L-verify-api/L-verify-completion. Four real Raft instances start with empty in-memory stores and default background workers. BootstrapCluster on the designated old peer creates a single-voter prefix and its actual timer-driven election. Successful sequential AddVoter, AddVoter and AddNonvoter calls create the final stable configuration. A real Apply completes; the harness waits for all FSMs to contain its value and all CommitIndex values to cross the configuration entry. Latest membership contents are checked using GetConfiguration; the configuration entry index is taken from the successful membership future, because GetConfiguration constructs no latestIndex. InmemTransport Disconnect cuts every cross-component direction. The replacement is observed through State/CurrentTerm and its actual successful Apply future before old VerifyLeader is invoked.
legality.applicability: One component contains the former leader and optionally its nonvoter link; the other contains the two other voters. Ordinary AppendEntries, heartbeats, elections, lease checks, FSM and snapshot workers all run. Newer-term negative replies from the majority are prevented by the network cut, not bypassed in protocol code. Old local lease is 2s, with 2s heartbeat/election timeouts; others use 100ms heartbeat, 150ms election and 80ms lease. CommitTimeout=5ms supplies frequent ordinary contact before the cut. Each Config is actually validated by NewRaft. Optional pipelining is declined via its supported ErrPipelineReplicationNotSupported fallback so all traffic follows the controlled in-memory routes. Counters only observe successful real RPC returns. In-memory storage represents a crash-free execution; it does not provide production durability evidence. The two subtests are independent complete histories, never concatenated into one.
unresolved: The result isolates a public contract discrepancy; exact vote-edge causality is supported by source and reply counters, not by instrumentation inside notifyAll.
Different configured node timeouts are intentional and scoped. No conclusion is made about a uniform-timeout deployment.
alternatives: The no-nonvoter-contact control leaves lease cleanup running and waits for actual verification completion rather than treating silence as failure.
Healthy connected verification must complete successfully before partition; failure aborts that history as an unreached prerequisite.

grounding.derivation: For O-verify-current-authority and L-verify-api/L-verify-completion, replacement_write records a successful actual Apply on a distinct elected peer at a term numerically greater than the old term. verify_invocation follows that event and selects the same replacement participant through an explicit predecessor reference. A generated op identifies the one invocation independently of term and success. verify_result records the actual Future.Error return as ok=(err==nil), plus raw term/state/FSM values. The oracle requires ok=false for this admitted obsolete-authority invocation. It does not require success merely because support might be sufficient, and does not infer general liveness from waiting.
grounding.applicability: Admission is verify_invocation after its correlated replacement_write, not the first prerequisite by order. Both histories keep the old peer cut off from the voting majority. Identity is op only; mutable terms, roles and results are not identity filters. The driver ends by waiting for the real future or declaring an incomplete deadline, then shuts all nodes down. Any failure in a prefix stops that history before admission. Healthy-control events are separate setup diagnostics, not prerequisites or results for this monitor.
unresolved: Raw old/new FSM values demonstrate the application states sampled around this API invocation; no separate externally served read API is executed.
Transport counts do not rule out every already-returned pre-partition reply being scheduled late, so they alone do not prove the exact cause.

observable_properties.description: After a real replacement leader completes its command before invocation, the isolated old peer must not return successful VerifyLeader assurance.

uncertainties: Only protocol v3, fixed three-voter/one-nonvoter membership, crash-free in-memory storage and nonpipelined transport are exercised.
All timeouts bound construction/observation only. An unreached prefix or missing return is unknown, not holds or a liveness finding.
Public verification failure in the no-contact control need not occur at an exact deadline or with an exact error string.
The two executions compare connectivity; their election terms, participants and replies are correlated only within each subtest.
This check does not claim invalid log commitment or a production application read violation.
